new_statements.citation: Hinton, Bryan. 2000. The languages of Wetar: recent survey results and word lists, with notes on Tugun grammar. In Charles E. Grimes (ed.), Spices from the East: papers in languages of eastern Indonesia, 105-129. Pacific Linguistics 503. Canberra: Australian National University. doi:10.15144/PL-503.105
new_statements.locator: p.119, Appendix B 'Comparative word lists', Symbols (PDF p.15); Aputai exceptional form p.127 item 178 (PDF p.23); editor's note p.119
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress in the Wetar languages, Aputai included, falls on the penultimate syllable; the survey word lists mark stress only where it deviates, and in the printed Aputai (Ilputih) list a single form is so marked (pik'pre 'spit', final stress). Monosyllables in the lists are to be read as like-vowel sequences (CVV), so they too are penultimate-stressed.
new_statements.exceptions: Deviations marked ad hoc with a preceding apostrophe in the word lists; for Aputai only pik'pre 'spit' (item 178). The clitic-induced shift to the root-final syllable (aspectual -e/-me) is described for Tugun only (sec. 6.2, pp.115-116), not for Aputai.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is a transcription convention covering elicited citation forms (survey word lists, 1988-1990) for all Wetar languages jointly; Aputai data = word list 3, Ilputih(b), one informant (Joseph Manuka, 37). Not an Aputai-specific phonological analysis; author later noted he had not recorded vowel length.
new_statements.identity_note: Hinton's Aputai data are word list 3, Ilputih(b) village (south-central coast of Wetar), informant Joseph Manuka; the Lurang (north-coast) Aputai community was not word-listed. The stress statement itself is a blanket one for all 'Wetar languages' (Perai, Aputai, Tugun, Ili'uun and Talur) in the Appendix B symbol key, not an Aputai-specific analysis; the same file and statement were already used for tugu1245 (Tugun) and iliu1237 (Ili'uun). Ethnologue/Wikipedia treat Aputai as one of four varieties of 'Wetarese'; Glottolog keeps aput1237 as a language (79-80% lexical similarity with Perai, pera1257... per Hinton p.113-114).

sources.note: p.119 Appendix B (Symbols, covering all five printed lists incl. Aputai = list 3, Ilputih(b)): 'Stress in Wetar languages is generally penultimate. It is marked with an apostrophe preceding the stressed syllable where different.' Only Aputai form so marked: pik'pre 'spit' (item 178, p.127, verified on page image). Editor's note p.119: monosyllables = like-vowel sequences, 'Word stress remains penultimate.' Sec. 6.2 pp.115-116 (Tugun only): penultimate, aspectual clitics -e/-me shift stress to root-final syllable.
